stablecoin_freeze_reconciliation.interpretation: The $823M TRM figure is an earlier incident snapshot; Reuters later reports Circle had frozen more than $1.1B USDC by November 2. These are successive measurements and must not be added. The $2.7B total frozen/rescued is a separate aggregate that includes multiple issuers and a network-governance intervention.

event_timeline.event: Bitquery reports approximately $6.3B left 17 Binance hot wallets across nine chains; the first identified major transfer was on XRPL.
TRM's timeline reports Circle froze approximately $823M USDC in the main Ethereum attacker wallet.
TRM reports Ripple froze approximately $40.5M RLUSD linked to the incident.
Binance resumed customer withdrawals in phases; Binance later said it had replenished or covered approximately 95% of affected assets and would cover customer losses.
Reuters reports $4.72B net customer outflows since Binance reopened, approximately 3% of platform assets; Binance reports $2.7B customer inflows since Sunday and stabilizing withdrawals.
Reuters reports Circle said it had frozen more than $1.1B in USDC linked to the hack, a later count than TRM's initial $823M snapshot.
The two 40M XRP transfers from the original attacker account form part of the original redistribution; they are not later outflows from the six recipient wallets.

data_quality_controls: Do not add Reuters' later >$1.1B USDC freeze to TRM's earlier $823M; they are successive counts.
Do not add the $2.7B frozen/rescued aggregate to the individual issuer freeze amounts; the aggregate already includes components.
Do not treat the $4.72B net customer outflow and $2.7B customer inflow as independent gross totals without matching windows and definitions.
Do not attribute OKX, Gate or Bybit inflows to Binance customers without wallet- or account-level evidence.
Do not equate Binance's reported 95% replenishment of affected assets with 95% recovery of stolen funds or 95% customer withdrawals.
Do not infer XRP-specific market outflows from exchange-wide net withdrawal totals.

source_records.observation: Published November 2 at 01:53 UTC. Reports $4.72B net Binance customer outflows since reopening (~3% of platform assets), Binance-reported $2.7B customer inflows since Sunday and stabilizing withdrawals, $6B company funds raised to cover losses, venue inflows at OKX/Gate/Bybit with uncertain origin, and Circle's statement that it had frozen >$1.1B USDC.
Reports $6.3B left 17 Binance hot wallets on nine chains, approximately $2.7B frozen/rescued, $729M USDT escaped before freezes and on-chain balances through 13:26 UTC November 2.
Early incident timeline includes Circle's approximately $823M USDC freeze and Ripple's approximately $40.5M RLUSD freeze; figures are earlier snapshots.

Recovery update #4; Binance reports phased withdrawal resumption and replenishment/coverage of affected assets. The announcement URL redirected to a generic support page in this retrieval, so exact 95% details are retained as previously retrieved company-reported claims, not newly reverified here.
Native XRP cannot be frozen or reversed by an issuer; issued tokens have different issuer control features.
